subject: Post-call recap: performance criteria & customer-led stress rehearsal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: performance criteria & next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before your team runs the customer-led stress rehearsal.

Summary of performance targets you confirmed on the call:
- P95 latency (text-generation, 512 token avg): <= 150 ms
- Max sustainable throughput: ~1,500 requests/sec (90% sustained for 10m windows)
- Concurrent active sessions (streaming): up to 220 simultaneous streams
- Streaming behavior: server-sent-chunks with <60 ms inter-chunk delay target and partial-token flushing enabled

Key constraints from your side:
- Test data will be synthetic but must preserve burstiness and 75% streaming sessions
- Your DevOps will run the k6 scenario from their CI runner using our test account

Proposed next steps (action owners):
1) Finlytics: share the k6/Locust scenario you plan to run (Samira/Amit) — we need the script by EOD tomorrow so we can validate headers and token usage.
2) Redwood (Monica): prepare a test API key (read-only quota) + short-lived pool credentials, and provide IP allowlist entries.
3) Redwood (Karthik/SEs): sanity-check the script for correct concurrency ramp and recommend batching/cache settings.
4) Both: agree on a 3-hour test window (weekend preferred) and rollback/fail criteria (too many 5xx or 99th spike).

I attached a minimal runbook and a sample k6 snippet we use for similar customers; Monica — can you provision the test key and IP allowlist template?

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivk.kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: stress-rehearsal-runbook-v1.md, sample_k6_snippet.js
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@finlytics.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance criteria & next steps

Thanks Vivek — all good on the targets, those look accurate. A few clarifications from our side:
- P95 target: we'll exercise both short (64 tokens) and medium (512 tokens) scenarios; please confirm we can label runs so we can separate results.
- For throughput, the 1,500 rps target is for steady-state; we'll do several 10-minute ramps and one long 30-minute soak at 1,200 rps.
- Streaming: our clients expect chunked partials for the first token to appear <200ms; we can accept slightly higher p95 for chunked sessions but would like guidance on expected tokenization overhead.

I've attached our initial k6 scenario (finlytics_k6_scenario_v1.js) — Amit will run it from our runner. Please review for header auth and any rate-limiting artifacts.

Proposed test window: Saturday 2026-12-05 02:00–05:00 UTC (our off-peak). Can you confirm Redwood AVAILABILITY then?

—Samira
Samira Khan
Product Lead, Finlytics
samira.k@finlytics.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T20:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance criteria & next steps (internal)

Looping us in to prepare infra. I pulled the attached k6 scenario and ran a smoke validation against staging with a replayed token to sanity-check auth headers. Findings:
- Script uses a tight 0s think time for streaming sessions; recommend a 5–10 ms think to avoid unrealistic full-concurrency spikes.
- Their script does not re-use connection pooling in one place (we see repeated TLS handshakes). We'll provide a small patch to keep-alive and connection reuse.

Action items for us:
- I will create a read-only test API key scoped to their deal and annotate it with run tags (finlytics-stress-20261205).
- Sean: can you open a short-lived allowlist for their runner IPs? They provided a CIDR block in the attached rls-allowlist-ips.txt.
- Karthik/SE: please review the runbook and provide suggested autoscale cushions (initial 2x buffer; add per-queue backpressure thresholds).

I'll draft the runbook changes and ping compliance for the temporary key TTL (24h).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: DevOps Team <devops@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@finlytics.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T22:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance criteria & next steps

Thanks Monica — attaching the CIDR list (rls-allowlist-ips.txt). A couple of notes from our side:
- Our runner pool is hosted in GCP us-west1 and will originate from 35.192.0.0/14 plus a few ephemeral ranges (included).
- We'll coordinate a one-hour dry-run (low RPS) on Friday 2026-12-04 to validate connectivity and keep-alive behavior. That dry-run will use 5 concurrent sessions as a smoke test.
- For data, we will seed synthetic prompts that respect your data-retention policy (no customer PII).

Let us know the test API key and any header changes you make so we can update the k6 script.

—DevOps (on behalf of Amit)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-04T07:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: performance criteria & next steps (internal)

Notes from runbook review:
- Recommended autoscale headroom: start with 2x baseline capacity and allow linear scale to 4x with a 5m scale cooldown. This gives room for the 1,500 rps target plus bursts.
- Tokenization overhead: advise Finlytics that medium-length requests (512 tokens) will show ~1.2x CPU/latency multiplier vs 64-token flows; suggest they weight their scenarios 60/40 short/medium.
- Streaming specifics: enable partial-token flush at 128-token intervals for medium flows to keep first-byte latency lower.

I pushed a small patch to the k6 snippet (keeps-alive + 8ms think-time for streaming loops) and attached it to the runbook. Monica, please create the key and drop the auth header example here once available.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>, DevOps Team <devops@finlytics.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-04T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: Test credentials + Saturday window confirmation

Samira — thanks for the fast turn. We've provisioned the test API key and attached the runbook with the k6 patch.

Credentials (sensitive — shared to Finlytics DevOps only):
- API Key: redwood-test-finlytics-20261205 (TTL: 24 hours)
- Base URL: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/test
- Run tags: finlytics-stress-20261205

Allowlist: we've whitelisted the CIDRs you provided for the window 2026-12-05T02:00:00Z — 2026-12-05T05:00:00Z. If you want an earlier dry-run window, confirm and we'll open the rule for Friday 2026-12-04 22:00–23:00 UTC.

Final ask before the run: please confirm you will do a Friday dry-run (5 concurrent) and whether the Saturday soak will be the 30-minute continuous soak at 1,200 rps followed by the 3x 10-minute ramps to 1,500 rps.

We will have SRE on standby during the Saturday window and will monitor token-level latency traces and 5xx errors; rollback if >2% 5xx over any 5m window.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
